description: AOE standard ontology catalog (PRD §6.15 / Stream 1 H.5). Each entry can resolve to either a bundled file (`source.kind = "bundled"`, `source.path` resolves under `backend/app/data/ontologies/`) or a remote URL (`source.kind = "url"`, `source.url`). The catalog importer prefers bundled when present and falls back to URL fetch otherwise.

ontologies.name: DCMI Metadata Terms
ontologies.description: Dublin Core Metadata Initiative Terms vocabulary -- the 15 legacy Dublin Core elements plus the most commonly used DCMI Terms. Bundled minimal subset suitable for offline catalog imports.

source.note: Hand-reduced subset of DCMI Metadata Terms — the 15 legacy elements plus the most commonly used terms — not the full upstream vocabulary.

ontologies.name: FOAF (Friend of a Friend)
ontologies.description: FOAF vocabulary describing people, their activities, and their relations to other people and objects. Common identity-modeling building block.

ontologies.name: SKOS Core
ontologies.description: Simple Knowledge Organization System -- W3C recommendation for representing thesauri, classification schemes, taxonomies, and subject heading systems.

ontologies.name: PROV-O
ontologies.description: W3C PROV Ontology -- represents and exchanges provenance information on the web. Activities, agents, entities, and their relationships.

source.note: Declared format was 'xml'; the server serves Turtle, so the URL import failed. Bundling pins both the bytes and the format.

ontologies.name: OWL-Time
ontologies.description: W3C ontology of temporal concepts -- instants, intervals, durations, temporal relationships. Useful base for any event/time-modeling ontology.

source.note: Declared format was 'xml'; the server serves Turtle, so the URL import failed. Bundling pins both the bytes and the format.

ontologies.name: Schema.org Core
ontologies.description: Schema.org full vocabulary -- structured data markup for web pages. Large vocabulary (~800 classes, ~1500 properties); imported as the full graph then optionally filtered by namespace.

source.note: Declares its types as rdfs:Class, not owl:Class. The importer read only owl:Class, so this entry imported ZERO of its advertised classes until that was fixed.

ontologies.name: FIBO Foundations: Agents
ontologies.description: FIBO (Financial Industry Business Ontology) Foundations module modelling agents (people, organizations, autonomous agents) within the financial industry.

ontologies.name: FIBO Foundations: Accounting
ontologies.description: FIBO Foundations accounting equity module -- core concepts for financial accounting.

ontologies.name: BFO 2020 (Basic Formal Ontology)
ontologies.description: ISO/IEC 21838-2 upper ontology. Its central division is continuant vs occurrent -- things that persist through time and are wholly present at each moment (a tyre, a vehicle, a sensor) versus things that unfold in time and have temporal parts (a fault event, a state transition, a maintenance procedure). Underneath that sit the distinctions that keep an extracted hierarchy honest: independent continuants (the bearers) against qualities, roles, dispositions and functions (what the bearers have, play, or are for). A speed rating is a quality of a tyre, not a kind of tyre -- BFO is where that difference is stated rather than assumed.

source.note: BFO 2020, the ISO-standardised revision. Deliberately not the 2019-08-26 BFO 2.0 that http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/bfo.owl still serves.

ontologies.name: SOSA/SSN (Semantic Sensor Network)
ontologies.description: W3C/OGC Recommendation for sensors, actuators and what they measure. Supplies the pattern a sensor reading needs and an extractor rarely invents: a Sensor makes an Observation, of an ObservableProperty, of a FeatureOfInterest, with a Result at a time. A tyre-pressure sensor is then a Sensor, pressure is an ObservableProperty, the tyre is the FeatureOfInterest, and each reading is its own Observation -- four distinct things where a flat extraction tends to produce one class called 'Tyre Pressure'. SSN adds System, Deployment and Procedure on top of the SOSA core.

source.license: W3C Software and Document License; OGC Software Notice
source.note: SOSA (http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/) and SSN merged into one document. SSN owl:imports SOSA and is close to useless without it, and the catalog importer parses a single document rather than following imports. Both owl:Ontology declarations are preserved.

ontologies.name: VSSo (Vehicle Signal Specification Ontology)
ontologies.description: The COVESA Vehicle Signal Specification expressed as an ontology: a standardised taxonomy of vehicle components and their observable and actuatable properties, from Powertrain and Chassis down to individual sensor and actuator signals. The core vocabulary supplies the structural relations -- Vehicle, VehicleComponent, partOf, partOfVehicle, belongsToVehicleComponent, and the Static/Dynamic/Observable/Actuatable VehicleProperty split -- so component containment is expressed as containment and a reading is a property of a component, rather than both being collapsed into rdfs:subClassOf. That collapse is the single most common way an extracted vehicle hierarchy goes wrong.

source.note: vsso-core.ttl (structural vocabulary) and vss_rel_2.2.ttl (generated component catalogue) merged into one document; either alone is half the ontology. Bundled rather than fetched because the published location is a gh-pages branch path.
